author: dallas city wire
title: SMU to send six swimmers to NCAA Championships in Atlanta this week
text:
Southern Methodist University will send six swimmers to the NCAA Championships in Atlanta starting Wednesday, March 24. The team will compete in four individual events and two relays, marking another milestone for a program with a history of 29 NCAA champions but none since 1998.
The participation highlights the continued progress of SMU’s men’s swimming and diving program. Head coach Greg Rhodenbaugh said, “It just means that our program is getting better and better and better. But you see that from the school records, there’s only one school record that we haven’t set since I’ve been here, but I coached the guy that holds it, so yeah, we’re getting better and better and better.”
Among those representing SMU is Berube, who holds two individual school records as well as being part of the record-holding 400 medley relay team. After narrowly missing out last year, he qualified for both the 100 and 200 backstroke events this season. “The goal over the summer was to put myself in a position to make NCAAs in the midseason,” Berube said. “When the midseason meet came around, I hovered around the 19th place marker (in the 200) until ACC came, where I then dropped another second from my midseason time and now sit 18th.” He also spoke about how having more teammates at nationals creates a positive environment: “A great group of six guys in the water at one point in time is uplifting and helps… And how many have qualified this year can send a message to everyone else on the team… ‘Hey, bring more guys. Take more steps forward.'”
Freshman Brennan will make his debut at NCAAs after qualifying for both the 200 and 500 freestyle events; he is SMU’s first freshman qualifier since 2009. He broke his own school record multiple times this season with his latest mark at 1:32.13 for the 200 freestyle event. “I usually go based off times,” Brennan said. “I find where you place is nice… but as long as you’ve done all you can to be better than you were before, you’ve got to be happy with yourself.” Coach Rhodenbaugh praised Brennan’s rapid development along with other freshmen.
Veterans Lockhart, Sungail, Forrest—and sophomore Likins—will join Brennan on relay teams aiming for strong finishes after earning All-America status last year in relays for SMU—the first such honor in over ten years according to Forrest: “When I was being recruited… our coaches told us that goal was to build SMU into a program competitive at NCAA level… So getting to spend my entire four years at SMU then be in position end at NCAA level is really cool for me.” Likins added about gaining early experience: “I think this will be a great experience for me leading into my next two years here… I think having this experience this year …will be great.”
Rhodenbaugh reflected on returning seven years ago aiming to rebuild competitiveness: “That was kind of whole idea coming back—just try get it back competitive toward Top Ten because that’s what I was used when here before …We’ve got ways go …but we’re accelerating quicker than wave so we’re catching it …We’ll be there next year or two.”
